one_star_reviews.text:
Absolutely disappointing experience.

I'm 23 years old and had eye surgery for myopia and astigmatism with intraocular lenses, paying €20,000, not including the tests. A year and a half later, my vision has deteriorated, and I requested a follow-up appointment.

After traveling almost two hours to the clinic, I was told that if I didn't pay €135 for the consultation, in addition to the tests, they wouldn't see me. I tried to speak with Dr. Elies, but he didn't even bother to come out; he simply told the receptionist that I had to pay first.

Furthermore, I got the feeling that the prices change depending on who treats you, which I find outrageous.

I'm a 23-year-old woman, and I can't keep paying whatever amount they ask for each time, especially after already paying €20,000 for the surgery. The saddest part is the helplessness of feeling that, if you have a problem after the operation, your only option is to complain, while the doctor seems completely unconcerned.

I thought that, in addition to finding a good professional, I would find humanity and concern for the patient. It has been a huge disappointment.

My myopia and astigmatism surgery with intraocular lenses cost €20,000, not including the tests. Before the operation, Dr. Elies was kind, approachable, and inspired confidence. But that image completely vanished when problems arose.

A year and a half later, I've lost vision and requested a follow-up appointment. The response was outrageous: the doctor didn't even come out to see me and simply stated that the visit would cost €135, as if the visual impairment had no relation whatsoever to the surgery. This attitude conveys indifference, a lack of responsibility, and zero interest in the patient's follow-up.

After surgery of this level and cost, the very least one can expect is serious and professional follow-up. My postoperative experience has been disappointing, and I believe the treatment I received falls far short of what is expected from a specialist in this field.

one_star_reviews.text:
It's the closest thing to an old-fashioned mental asylum, but since money seems to be the only thing that matters here, let me tell you something:

Juan Torres and his cronies never turn away a patient, even if they're completely stable, because of the lucrative business MUFACE (the civil servants' mutual insurance fund) represents and its per-patient payments. It works out perfectly for them: they overmedicate the patient, make them feel guilty when perhaps they haven't done anything wrong and shouldn't even be there, and the fresh cash flows into their pockets and the center's coffers.

Clearly, it's all about money, isn't it?

This hospital used to be good, the doctors are wonderful, but the reception staff is terrible. It's shameful. People like these shouldn't work here. We need people with heart here. At the Seranil clinic, they never leave you waiting on hold for a call, not even for a minute. Here, they never answer, and if they do, they leave you waiting on the phone for six to seven minutes. People like this shouldn't work at the reception desk. We deserve better service. Parents and family members, our children need us all the time. They wouldn't let me speak to my daughter today because, according to them, she had already received a call. It feels like a dictatorship here. In the century we live in, limited calls are a disgrace. The receptionist's service is shameful.

one_star_reviews.text:
Extremely disappointing and unacceptable experience with Alamo Valladolid.
I made a prepaid reservation for €146 for a 7-seat automatic Seat Alhambra or similar. When I arrived, I was told that there were no 7-seat vehicles left.
Instead of providing an equivalent vehicle, I was given two options: pay an additional fee for a Toyota with 8 seats, or take a smaller 5-seat vehicle with absolutely no refund or price adjustment.
So essentially, despite having a fully paid reservation, I was offered either to pay more or to accept a significantly smaller vehicle without receiving any compensation.
This is not the level of service I expected from an international rental company. A prepaid reservation should mean something, and customers should not be left paying more because the reserved vehicle is no longer available.
I have requested a full refund of the amount that i paid and a clear explanation of how this situation was handled.
I strongly recommend that Alamo management review what happened at this location. This is not an acceptable way to handle a prepaid reservation.

one_star_reviews.text: I went to a gynecologist appointment and it lasted a full 7 minutes, from start to finish, and cost 130 euros. In those 7 minutes, she obviously couldn't detect anything, if I had anything wrong. She asked very few questions, and only the most basic ones. The whole thing was very impersonal, especially since it was my first time seeing a gynecologist. I don't like to leave bad reviews, but this shows a lack of interest in patients, few recommendations for prevention related to exercise and diet, and nothing about pelvic floor exercises when I experience urinary incontinence while training. I went to another gynecologist who performed a breast ultrasound, had a much longer appointment, offered recommendations, and treated me with kindness and care, because above all, we are people. It was a completely different experience. I don't recommend this doctor at all, and on top of that, the other gynecologist detected things that this one didn't. I have friends who have had the same experience.

I don't like to leave negative reviews; in fact, I prefer not to write anything at all.

But in this case, I think it's necessary because any couple can go through the same thing. It's hard and expensive.

Our first visit to IERA was perfect. We left happy, thinking that in a few months we would be pregnant. We requested partial funding for the estimate, and everything was starting. At the second appointment, everything changed. The results started coming back negative, and they even began suggesting we do more tests, specifically the Fragile X test, to ensure the future baby wouldn't have an intellectual disability. According to my blood tests, I could be a carrier, based on my low AMH level. When I refused, things changed. They made me sign that same document at practically every appointment I had at IERA. The strange thing is that I never felt they could retrieve an egg from me because there wasn't even an attempt, which I'll explain later.

But they wanted to do the test. It wasn't free, obviously.

I'm 37, athletic, have always eaten well, and have low AMH.

What options did they have for me? Or rather, one of their gynecologists said so.

Egg donation.

My question in every single appointment I had there—because we barely spoke again with the gynecologist we started with—wasn't there anything that could help change the situation?
Their answer: NO. Appointment after appointment.
There was a point when I would travel (about 200 km round trip from where I live), it happened up to three times, they would count my follicles and send me home, without any treatment, stimulation, or anything.
There was only one attempt at stimulation, which they canceled after four days.

Seeing no progress, no treatment, and not even any interest from them, we decided to cancel the treatment. We were wasting time and money. That's how it felt.

And we weren't wrong.

Everything was paid for as we went along (tests, analyses, etc.) right there, as we left the appointment, without touching the financing money.

They decided not to refund the full amount of the financing, demanding an outstanding balance for which, to this day, we still haven't received an invoice or a breakdown. And we did NOT sign any estimate.
So, without permission or prior notice, they decided to take that amount from our financing. We only realized this when the finance company refunded us the entire amount of the unused portion of the payments we had already made.

Sad, disappointed, and with too much money literally thrown away, we decided to go to Ginemed in Seville.
Everything changed. Treatment began on day one via video call. (Supplements to improve egg quality)
When they asked me basic questions, like when I started menstruating (16 years old), something they never asked me at IRA, they understood that I started late, hence my low AMH level. They're not worried about Fragile X syndrome, therefore.
First visit, follicle count, they tell me I have 10, I can't believe it. At IERA, there were 3 or 4 follicles and no home treatment; theoretically, they weren't expecting more because my AMH was low.

Currently, thanks to Ginemed, I'm 9 weeks pregnant with a heartbeat. With my own eggs and no problems. Everything went perfectly the first time.
My personal recommendation: avoid IERA if you want to become a mother.

I'm not giving it fewer stars because Google won't let me.

My experience with this real estate agency has been quite disappointing. The fees were paid upfront, and yet, on the day of the sale, no one from the agency showed up at the notary's office, even though I had been told beforehand that one of the responsible people would be there.

During the process, I also had to personally handle and manage many documents and procedures, something I believe should be part of the service for which I'm paying a fee.

To make matters worse, problems arose at the notary's office with the property tax (IBI) that should have been clarified and coordinated with both parties beforehand. What I had agreed upon with the buyer didn't match what she claimed to have discussed with the agency.

Frankly, if I have to do most of the paperwork myself, and then when the most important moment of the transaction arrives, no one shows up, I wonder what kind of service I'm paying for. To do practically the same thing, I might as well sell the apartment myself and save the fees.

Very little involvement, very little communication, and management that, in my opinion, doesn't live up to their fees. I wouldn't use this real estate agency again, nor would I recommend it.

one_star_reviews.text: Beware, these are scammers! First, they hook you in by saying you'll be doing work from home, like assembling pens. Once you send them in, they promise to pay you for the work. Meanwhile, they add you to a fake Telegram group and ask you to "like" a series of articles to increase their online visibility and boost sales. They claim you'll be paid €7/day for these "likes," but you only receive one payment until you complete another challenge: buying an item ranging from €35 to over €300. That's where the scam comes in. They tell you they'll refund the purchase price plus a percentage of what you spent. The group constantly repeats the same messages, supposedly from other members, but the same comments appear every morning, making you believe they're from different members encouraging you to buy. Logically I didn't do it, I realized it was a scam and of course the pens never arrived and they never let me participate in the telegram group, you can't make any comments, that's why you can only read without participating so nobody can expose the scam.

one_star_reviews.text:
I DO NOT RECOMMEND THIS CLINIC. Our experience has been very negative, and after what happened with my father, we have completely lost confidence in it.

My father had been receiving treatment at TECNOLASER Cádiz for years, attending regular checkups and even undergoing several ophthalmological procedures. Among them, he had cataract surgery in both eyes and was later treated to try to reduce his astigmatism through incisions, without achieving the expected result.

After one of these procedures, he continued to experience significant visual discomfort and eye pressure problems for months. Despite returning to the clinic and stating that he was still having problems, we received neither an explanation nor a solution that put our minds at ease.

Given the persistence of the symptoms, we decided to seek a second opinion at another ophthalmological clinic in Cádiz.

Our surprise and concern were enormous when, after performing the corresponding tests, he was diagnosed with severe glaucoma in one eye and moderate glaucoma in the other. As we have been told, the damage to one of his eyes is already very significant, and the visual prognosis is worrying.

As a family, we find it very difficult to understand how, after years of ophthalmological follow-up, frequent check-ups, and several procedures, a condition of this severity had not been detected previously.

We find it especially concerning that certain tests designed to assess the condition of the optic nerve and detect possible damage consistent with glaucoma had not been performed earlier, especially considering my father's age, medical history, and eye pressure problems.

I do not intend to determine through this review whether or not there has been medical negligence, because that should be assessed by the relevant professionals and, if necessary, through a review of his entire medical record.

But I can share what we have experienced: my father was followed for years at this clinic, and when he later went to another center for his vision problems, he was diagnosed with very advanced glaucoma.

This has been a devastating experience for us, and we believe that every patient has the right to know about our experience before deciding where to entrust something as important as their vision.

Therefore, I personally do not recommend TECNOLASER Cádiz and would advise any patient with persistent symptoms, concerns about their condition, or risk factors to seek a second opinion and ensure that all necessary tests are performed.

We are gathering the medical documentation and waiting to see how my father's condition progresses before deciding on the next steps.

I am sharing this experience because, as his daughter, I believe it is important for other families to be able to make informed decisions about the health of their loved ones.

We all used to go there to renew our licenses, but with this, they've lost four customers forever.

Terrible service. I had an appointment for a 20-second ultrasound (eco20) through Adeslas a month ago, but between booking and attending the appointment, my insurance company was switched to Asisa, which I had requested. Therefore, I called a week before the appointment to verify there would be no coverage issues. The receptionist told me there was no problem, and that when I arrived, I should show my new card and update my information. So, on the day of the appointment, October 6, 2026, at 10:00 AM, I arrived, and after providing all my information, the receptionist told me there was a problem: Asisa wouldn't cover the 20-second ultrasound. I told her that since I was already there, I'd like to see if she could do a regular follow-up appointment, as I had called to ask if Asisa covered the ultrasound and was told there was no problem. I consulted with the doctor, and he told me no, that Asisa doesn't cover consultations either, and that if I want to be seen, I have to pay for the consultation privately. It's shameful. I had called in advance to ask. They made me travel from El Puerto de Santa María to Jerez for nothing, and I missed my ultrasound appointment, which is one of the most important. Now I have to figure out where to get it done without missing the deadline. THANK YOU VERY MUCH for your professionalism and customer service (because in private practice, we are clients, not patients). I hope many people read this review and see how shameless this clinic is. Best regards.

EDIT after the clinic's response: THEY'RE LYING! I called!! I called before going to the appointment to ask about Asisa coverage, and the answer was that there was no problem. That's why I went. I was informed once I was there that Asisa didn't cover the consultation. On top of everything, they're liars...

one_star_reviews.text: Yesterday I went to the funeral of a family friend, and while I was waiting there for the hearse to arrive, I came across a shocking scene that shouldn't be happening, especially not in a cemetery. Up above, I saw a man sitting on a bench, drinking beer, singing as if he were alone, barefoot, and looking very unwell. This man stayed there for quite a while. Why don't they kick him out of the cemetery? It gives a terrible impression, and what is a man doing in those circumstances in a cemetery? Are there no security guards at the cemetery? Apparently not. First, they should kick this man out, since it's not the place for him to be there, especially the way he was. Second, it gave me the creeps that anything could happen to us while visiting our loved ones and nobody would even notice. And lastly, the cemetery is very neglected. Some of the stairs are very difficult for people with mobility problems to go up and down. It looked very run down. Why is it like this? Those stairs are terrible, beyond awful. It should be a peaceful and safe place, and it isn't, for all the reasons described. Fix everything properly and don't let drunk people into the cemetery, since it's not the place for them. I've never seen anything like what I experienced yesterday at this cemetery. I left very disappointed. FROM THIS CEMETERY.

I strongly recommend thinking twice before booking with this agency.

The property we were given was dirty, neglected and clearly not properly prepared for guests. The kitchen, cupboards and other areas were dirty, basic essentials such as soap and even a bathroom bin were missing, and the bed linen was not properly provided when we arrived.

The advertised double bed was only around 1 metre wide. The advertised coffee machine was not actually provided as expected, and instead of proper air conditioning for the property, there was only a portable unit.

The whole house felt old, neglected and almost abandoned. It was shocking that an agency could hand over a property to guests in this condition without properly checking and preparing it beforehand.

We paid for a comfortable holiday accommodation, but instead spent our time dealing with problems that should never have existed in the first place. Our holiday was seriously affected.

Based on our experience, I cannot recommend this agency and would never book with them again.

one_star_reviews.text:
After many years of traveling from Madrid for my annual checkups, for the first time I left disappointed, stressed, and with a thousand unanswered questions. It's a shame that time eventually leads to overcrowding, and doctors become more eager to see the next patient than to show empathy and patience to the one they're treating. I should mention that I wasn't seen by my usual doctor, but by a doctor I didn't know at all. She gave me a diagnosis that I didn't even have time to process. While I was getting dressed, a thousand questions, doubts, and fears flooded my mind, but she was already with the next patient and couldn't see me. I returned from Madrid the following Tuesday to see my usual doctor, hoping that he would not only clarify my doubts but also perform the test that the other doctor had recommended, given that he has been treating me for over 10 years. He cleared up my doubts, although his tone was certainly not the same as on other occasions; in fact, he seemed rather annoyed by so many questions. He recommended that I find another place where they could do the test sooner, as things couldn't wait, it seemed cancerous, and there I would have to wait at least three weeks for the biopsy results. I asked if I could have it done that day or the next, since he said the test only takes 15 minutes, and I've been traveling from Madrid for 10 years, but he said no.
I had to pick up the phone and start calling all the places that came up in Madrid to see which one could do it sooner. Finally, I found the Nuestra Señora del Rosario Hospital. They were kind and quick; in one week they confirmed the cancer diagnosis. They also found a second nodule that neither of the two doctors in Bologna saw, and it's also cancerous. I will not return to Bologna, and I certainly will never recommend it again.

Dear GNG, I am writing to file a formal complaint regarding the service I received on Monday, August 17, 2026, at your Santurtzi location.
I visited the store in person to request a quote for replacing the rear tires on my vehicle. From the outset, I explained to the employee that I wanted specific tires. After asking me about my annual mileage and providing the requested information, he indicated that, in his opinion, the tires were too good for my mileage and that it would be better to choose more economical options.
I fully understand that a professional can recommend alternatives based on vehicle usage, but I believe the final decision on which tires to install rests with the customer. When I stated that I wanted to stick with my choice, I perceived a lack of receptiveness and a disapproving expression from the employee.
Furthermore, I specifically requested a wheel alignment. The employee initially told me it wasn't necessary. I explained that I still wanted to proceed and the reasons why I felt it was necessary. When I insisted, their response was literally: "I'll send it to you tomorrow if that's the case."
As of today, Wednesday, August 19th, two days have passed and I still haven't received any quote or communication from the establishment.
I believe this situation demonstrates a lack of attention and interest towards a customer who came to the establishment intending to contract several services. It doesn't seem reasonable to me that, after requesting a quote in person and clearly specifying the services I wanted, I haven't received any proposal or been contacted.
I hope this will be taken into account to improve customer service.

The reception and rehabilitation staff were excellent.

He ordered an MRI between rehabilitation sessions, despite the presence of fluid and inflammation. He prescribed four days of anti-inflammatories and discharged me, noting in the report that there was pain upon palpation. He never even bothered to examine my hand. Obviously, if the pain was still there after three months, four days of anti-inflammatories wasn't going to make it go away. And of course, here I am, still in pain and with a false discharge, since he assured me that would resolve it, but it didn't.
Furthermore, on my first visit, he was over an hour late, even though the waiting room was empty. It was disrespectful, especially since I was with my daughter because it was summer and I had nowhere else to leave her. I wouldn't recommend this doctor to my worst enemies. If you can, avoid him. Don't go.

I'm really disappointed with the service. I've been to many centers for injuries, but this is the first time this has happened to me. They only offer one session per week, which goes against recovery.

I had to file a complaint for hidden defects, and my lawyer has taken everything to court. After I deregistered as self-employed, they decided not to give me the file for the years 2024, 2025, and 2026. They told me they couldn't find it, and they won't give it to me because, in addition, they didn't include the expenses I pay them monthly in the relevant box on my tax return. I'm going to the tax office on Monday with the I have the tax return they submitted to me and the receipts for the payments I've been religiously making to them monthly for their work. My lawyer will, of course, take the appropriate measures. I absolutely do not recommend this agency; they are unprofessional and, without a doubt, liars. NI NAIZ JOXE ATXEGA GARCIA. Anyone who needs proof of what I'm saying, I can show it to them so they don't make the same mistake I did.

one_star_reviews.text:
A complete renovation began in March 2022. In December 2022, I was forced to consider the project closed, even though some things were still pending, as they stopped responding to my inquiries. Problems arose from the very beginning: they removed the alarm system, worth hundreds of euros, and left it on the balcony; they urinated in the toilet even though there was no water, leaving it unused for days without flushing a single bottle of water. Even after removing the drain, they told me I didn't need rubble bags because they would take everything away the same day they delivered the materials, but then they left a pile of bags in the street for over a week. The tiles are poorly laid; I broke two of the door handles just days after they were installed; the shower wasn't properly sealed and water leaked out… You couldn't do so many things wrong if you were intentional. The documentation for the installed equipment is nowhere to be found. To top it all off, they haven't given me the invoice I've been requesting since August. It's clear he's trying to keep the VAT money, leaving me unable to justify the expenses for energy efficiency improvements or claim the warranty if any appliance malfunctions. Of course, I've already filed a complaint.

If you're reading this because you're considering hiring this company, RUN! Find someone with even a modicum of professionalism and decency.

Four years later, I get a message from Google saying the content can't be published, who knows why. I have proof of everything explained here. He didn't issue an invoice, keeping the VAT money. He's a THIEF who should be in jail.

one_star_reviews.text:
My experience with Global Entrenucleos has been very disappointing, as has my experience with Andrés Barrado Vicente. I bought a home in the Villas de Entrenúcleos cooperative, marketed by this company. Two years after the members moved into our homes, we still don't have a permanent electricity supply and are living with temporary construction power.

In my opinion, this situation could have been avoided if the necessary arrangements had been made well in advance to ensure all essential services were available when we moved into the homes.

The cooperative has contacted Global Entrenúcleos on numerous occasions to try to resolve this problem, but after two years, the situation remains practically unchanged. This has generated great frustration and uncertainty among all the affected families.

Furthermore, maintaining a home for so long with a temporary electricity supply and without the corresponding occupancy permit creates an additional worry: it could affect the terms and coverage of our home insurance, especially in serious situations like a fire. I don't think it's right that families have to endure this uncertainty after living in our homes for two years.

I'm writing this review so that anyone considering buying a property from this company can learn about our experience and carefully consider all these aspects before making a decision.

I sincerely hope this problem is resolved as soon as possible and that no other family has to live with a service interruption for years.

one_star_reviews.text:
THE WORST EXPERIENCE AT A HEALTH CENTER.

Last week I went to this clinic for CO2 laser treatment. The gynecological care was fine, but when I left and went to Reception to pay the bill, the following happened: The young woman at the counter informed us that the card machine wasn't working (it must "fail" frequently, judging by other reviews) and that they only accepted cash. My husband, who was with me, told her that we didn't have that amount (€174), but that we would pay via Bizum or bank transfer. The receptionist (visibly nervous) went into an office marked "Management," and a woman (to put it politely) came out and rudely told us to make an "immediate" transfer. My husband had to go outside because the cell phone reception in the clinic is very poor. When the bank confirmed that the transfer had been made, we went back to the woman at Reception, and she told us to wait because the computers weren't "working properly." After several minutes, and quite fed up with the situation, we told them we were leaving and that they should check on us and call us if anything changed. She went back into the management office, and then the "manager," or whatever she was, came out and, with a very arrogant attitude, called my husband a "clown." My husband demanded she identify herself, to which she replied that "a guy with an ear piercing wasn't going to bother."
We asked for the official complaint form, and they gave us one of their own, without a letterhead or number. I never thought I would suffer such degrading and humiliating treatment, especially in a place of health and respect like a medical clinic.
Reading the number of negative reviews about the appalling treatment this "lady" gives, I can't understand how someone like that can work in a healthcare center (or even a greengrocer's), unless their goal is to lose patients.
If they put a cave troll in the "Manager" position, they'd do a much better job.

This morning I called to schedule an appointment, and the employee who answered was incredibly rude and disrespectful. When I explained that I wanted to make an appointment, she responded rudely and hung up on me. I don't understand how someone like that can work with the public. Never go to that clinic after seeing how they treat patients.

one_star_reviews.text:
Negative Review

My experience has been very disappointing, and frankly, I feel cheated.

We are carrying out some work in Clariana de Cardener and have had a significant amount of diesel fuel consumption. Before deciding where to refuel, I spoke with the manager, Carme, who told me that, given the volume of fuel we were going to use, I would receive a discount.

Trusting her, I continued refueling at this station and didn't look for another gas station, precisely because I understood that the discount would be honored.

After waiting several days, the response was finally that a direct discount cannot be offered and that it had to be approved.

What I find unacceptable is that a commercial offer is made to the customer, who then makes decisions based on it and generates a significant volume of consumption, only to then be told that the discount cannot actually be applied.

If they had told me from the beginning that they couldn't guarantee any discount, I would have been free to compare with other stations and probably would have refueled elsewhere.

I don't question the existence of internal policies; what I question is making a commitment to a customer without having the capacity or authorization to fulfill it.

I find this a very unprofessional way to treat a customer who has made a considerable purchase and who trusted the manager's word.

My experience was negative, and I won't be refueling there again. I believe any customer should know that before trusting a promised discount, it's best to demand written confirmation.

one_star_reviews.text:
A friend's relative was rejected for treatment for alcoholism and ended up having to go to the bar to drink with her.

Shameful.

I spent two weeks hospitalized on the Aurora ward for a suicide attempt, despite having an eating disorder, and no one read my medical history to determine how to treat me. During those two weeks, the psychiatrist saw me a total of two times; one session was decent, and the other was fleeting. The psychologist is completely clueless; I'd tell her something, and the next day she'd ask me about the same thing. There are no daily visits with family members, and for the first few days, you can only have a measly 14-minute phone call with them, even though the schedule says "calls 6:00-7:00 PM." When I complained about this, the psychiatrist said it's because there are so many people, so the call time runs for an entire hour, giving each person only 14 minutes, which I find unacceptable.

The only therapeutic resource available practically every hour is so-called occupational therapy, and as a patient with experience from other hospitalizations, I can tell you it has nothing to do with what occupational therapy actually is. They do it every spare moment they have, and they've prioritized quantity over quality, since all they do are "cognitive worksheets to stimulate the brain," which weren't even personalized for each case but were generic, while the therapists openly complained about their work as if we couldn't hear them. All they wanted was to "keep us entertained" because all they did were those worksheets and the occasional craft activity.

Furthermore, my first contact with the nursing staff was very unpleasant. It was with a nurse/assistant named Blanca, who is very unpleasant, insensitive, and rude. I had a truly awful experience with her.
Regarding the eating disorder, they had no idea how to treat me, and even though I hadn't been admitted for that reason, they had to monitor me. I relapsed thanks to them because of their lack of control over my food intake; the only measures they took were to lock me in the bathroom for two hours after each meal and not let me brush my teeth except right before meals, which makes absolutely no sense. My parents insisted until they implemented a stricter protocol because if things continued as they were, I was going to end up malnourished for the third time. They kept telling my parents I was perfectly fine and improving, when in reality that wasn't the case.
If you recognize me, I don't mind. I hope you know who I am and that this center gradually declines, since all it does is worsen patients' conditions.

Subject: Urgent attention needed: Unreliable Mugi machines are costing passengers triple.
Bilbao Intermodal is a fantastic station—it is exceptionally clean, has very helpful staff, and offers a great cafeteria space. However, using the Mugi and Avanza services here has become an incredibly problematic experience.The automatic Mugi card top-up machines inside the terminal are frequently out of service. When these terminals fail, you cannot access the discounted Mugi fare of around €5. Instead, you are forced to pay the standard cash fare of nearly €14 just to travel to Donostia. This machine malfunction is completely unwarranted and unfairly costs passengers triple the price.
Advice to travellers: Never rely on the station's Mugi machines. The only dependable alternative at the station is to top up using a Kutxabank ATM, so ensure you carry a debit or credit card with sufficient funds.
A long-standing systemic issue: This lack of reliability and support is a pattern. Last year, an automatic machine in Vitoria-Gasteiz swallowed my personal Mugi card on a Friday. Station staff informed me no technician was available over the weekend. When I returned on Monday, the office claimed they could not find my card anywhere.
The operators must address these infrastructure failures and poor support protocols immediately.

one_star_reviews.text: The administrative and telephone system leaves much to be desired; it's impossible to get through. You have to take time off work to go there and be seen in person, and on top of that, they can't give you an appointment, so you have to wait days for them to call you back. As professionals, the psychological care is very good, although, like everything in the public healthcare system, it's slow and has a long waiting list, but that's not the center's fault, but rather the fault of the public healthcare system.

Terrible service, zero empathy, and professional negligence.
The care at the Molins de Rei Child and Adolescent Mental Health Center (CSMIJ/CSM) is appalling. During my appointment, after honestly explaining my situation, they showed complete indifference to my distress, leaving me unattended and rudely telling me to call an ambulance. Furthermore, while they themselves are constantly running late, if a patient is five minutes late, they cancel the appointment and postpone it for months.
The psychological treatment deserves special mention. There is one professional with whom several of us have had terrible experiences. In my case, when I was overwhelmed and crying during appointments, her response was to remain completely silent and offer no help. I also know of a patient with an eating disorder (ED) whom this same psychologist downplayed after days of not eating, which ended in a serious fainting spell.
To make matters worse, we have been pointing out my brother's difficulties for a long time so that he can be assessed and given the appropriate tests, but they just assign him painting classes without any serious follow-up.

one_star_reviews.text:
I absolutely do not recommend this clinic, especially because of my experience with Dr. Maletska.

The reception staff is very friendly and attentive. However, the doctor was unfriendly and, above all, made a diagnostic error.

I went there because I had sensitivity in one of my teeth, especially when eating. I didn't have pain, just sensitivity.

The doctor explained that the problem was related to the nerve and gave me a quote of €790, which included a root canal, crown reconstruction with posts or pins, and later a temporary crown and a metal-ceramic crown or bridge.

I decided to get a second opinion from another dentist. The other dentist performed a much more thorough examination, with an X-ray and a CT scan, and confirmed that the problem was not related to the nerve and that I didn't need a root canal or a crown. The filling simply needed to be redone.

They did the filling, and since then, I no longer have any sensitivity, and my tooth is perfectly fine.

I don't think it's normal that I was offered a €790 treatment, and especially that they made such a wrong diagnosis when my tooth was perfectly healthy.

I do not recommend this clinic.

one_star_reviews.text:
My experience with Dr. Marta García del Real has been disappointing regarding ultrasound follow-up.

In a check-up performed in May 2026, my file included the description of "uterus fibroids," but no measurements, location, or characteristics of the fibroids were recorded, nor was I advised to follow up on this finding.

Months later, after continuing to experience symptoms and undergoing a new gynecological evaluation, several fibroids were identified, one of them approximately 5 cm, in addition to an endometrial polyp. I was ultimately scheduled for a laparoscopic myomectomy.

When I requested the information from the May ultrasound to compare the changes, I discovered that there are no measurements that would allow me to know the size of the fibroids at that time.

I fully understand that findings can change and that not everything requires immediate intervention, but I believe that, considering my situation and the hormonal treatment I was receiving, it would have been important to properly document the fibroids and establish some type of follow-up.

I'm sharing my experience because I believe it's important for patients to know how to request that these types of findings be properly recorded so they can be compared in subsequent reviews.

one_star_reviews.text: I tried to schedule an appointment with her, but she wouldn't give me a quote for the consultations, even though I told her I was traveling alone and it would be online. She said the first consultation was €60 and that we would discuss the rest during the consultation, depending on my case. I asked her what it depended on, and she said we would discuss it. Terrible care home, understaffed, outdated facilities, chaotic organization. Some call it the "zombie home" because most of the residents spend their days sleeping.
We had a terrible experience. Like every week, we went to visit a relative. She was alone, sitting asleep in a corner, and looked very unwell. We called the doctor, who referred her to the hospital. When we arrived, they told us she was near death, and she passed away a few days later.
I'm left with many questions. Didn't any staff member see her condition? Isn't there anyone checking on these people sitting in those rooms?
The director doesn't seem to interact with anyone, locked away in her office with the blinds drawn... and doesn't want to be disturbed.
It's depressing how our elderly are treated. I urge the authorities to ensure the proper care of these people we call seniors, and who one day we will all be.

Being from a rural area is quite problematic because of the lack of services. And because the few services that are available monopolize the business, and that's just how it is. I've been asking this driving school for days, trying to understand what I can do if I can't attend classes because public transport, combined with the fact that the driving school only has classes from 7 to 8 pm, makes it impossible for me to get there. They don't have any kind of virtual classroom; they offer you a paid app to take tests, when there are several completely free ones on the Google Play Store. Since they don't have a virtual classroom, paying for a theory course that I won't be able to take seemed like a waste of money. So I asked for a price to do the theory test on my own and the practical test with them. And it turns out they charge the same price for the theory course, even 60 euros more 😂 if you do the theory test independently. Oh well. And since they're the only driving school in five surrounding towns, they can easily offer this kind of practical training. Anyway.
They don't have class times that a working person can adapt to. They don't have a virtual classroom, and if you pass the theory test on your own, the practical training with them ends up costing more than if you pay for the whole course. Anyway...

The worst private health insurance company by far. And I've experienced it twice.
For years I paid the maximum premium, and when you need them, they cover nothing. They don't always have specialists available. The service is very precarious and sporadically inadequate. My father needed them after a lifetime of paying into the company, and when he got cancer, they abandoned him.
They referred me to the General Hospital of Catalonia because they didn't have emergency specialists, and when they were going to do the neurology tests, they told me no and to go back to them (the private health insurance company). An inhumane mess.
My review is clear: IF YOU DON'T WANT TO BE CHEATED AND LEFT STRANDED, DON'T JOIN THIS INSURANCE COMPANY.

At the Granollers health insurance clinic, the service is terrible in many departments. In the last one I visited recently, the assistant was completely out of it, chattering away and ignoring the phone, which kept ringing in the waiting room. Even the doctor mentioned it. The doctor was very nice, but the assistant, with her airs of superiority, completely ignored her. The patients in the waiting room questioned her behavior. It's a disgrace. The waiting lists in some departments are shameful, and the restrooms... they could really use a facelift. I'm glad I cancelled my membership, like so many others, because it's not what it used to be. The service is a zero. I'm forced to give it one star, but it doesn't deserve any.

one_star_reviews.text: Waits of more than an hour

Terrible and rude service at reception.

I went to the medical center and Carla, the receptionist at the entrance, treated me in an extremely rude and unprofessional manner. When I told her my name, she immediately said, "You don't have an appointment." I assured her that I had it noted down, and without looking me in the eye or checking anything in the system, she replied curtly, "Well, it's not here. That doctor doesn't see patients on Tuesdays, so it can't be."
After checking my email, I discovered that the center had changed my appointment from Tuesday to Thursday. When I tried to calmly show her the email to clarify the situation, she interrupted me, saying she was attending to someone and that I should wait. When I showed her the email and calmly suggested that they could have called me to notify me of the change, her response was, "They probably called you, but we can't be calling all morning; if you don't answer, we'll send an email."
I don't find this response acceptable or professional. I was right; the original appointment existed, and the error was on their part. An absolute lack of empathy and public manners.
The waiting times are insane

one_star_reviews.text: This clinic was recommended to me, the first one I would visit, and they cancelled my first appointment twice. The first time was because they don't do initial consultations on Fridays, and then after they called me twice to confirm the appointment and sent another email hours before the appointment, they cancelled it again. Very unprofessional.

SECOND PREGNANCY
We were going through the process and informed Dr. Herrero that we had a trip planned, and that if we didn't have a period, we would wait. He told us there wouldn't be a problem and that we could do it a few days before the trip. To our surprise, it ended up being the same day we had to catch the plane. He told us not to worry, that we would do it first thing in the morning. What a surprise! He arrived an hour later than agreed! Naturally, we already knew that this attempt wasn't going to work; we were too nervous.
In the second attempt, everything was normal, and we got a positive beta test! The first appointment arrived, and it wasn't Dr. Herrero who saw us, but Dr. Illán, as usual, more than an hour late. They did the ultrasound and told us to come back the following week to make sure everything was progressing well (my partner found this a bit strange, since with the previous pregnancy, once they saw the gestational sac, they discharged us from the clinic). We went back the following week, and the same thing happened. Dr. Illán saw us, showed us in, and her face was priceless; she didn't know what to say. They moved us to a different room and ultrasound machine because she said the image wasn't clear. She then called Dr. Herrero, and they told us the gestational sac looked smaller than the previous week. They informed us that we had had a miscarriage. That same day, I had blood work done because I was injecting Neupogen and had to get it done every few days. I also had a beta-hCG test done at that appointment. We asked Dr. Illán if it wouldn't be better to wait for the beta-hCG results and not stop all the medication without knowing the results. She told us no, to stop all the medication, and said, "I'm so sorry, ladies, you've had a miscarriage." She also mentioned that the embryo might still be in the fallopian tubes, and if so, we would have to go to the hospital for emergency surgery. We were in shock! Back home, something told us we had to go to the hospital; we weren't convinced by what we'd just been told. Do you know what the surprise was? THERE WAS A HEARTBEAT! The next day, we called CRA requesting a report with everything they'd told us the day before, and naturally, they never sent us anything. We sent another email explaining the situation, and Dr. Herrero called us right away to come to the clinic. But it was too late to complain! Our daughter was born in January, and we're still waiting for the clinic to call us with the questionnaire they give to all the births there—how little empathy!
On top of all this, I should point out that we froze the sperm from our first pregnancy, and at no point were we informed that since six babies had already been born, we couldn't use it for this new pregnancy. If we had known, we would have started the freezing process much sooner. We requested the characteristics of the second donor repeatedly, and they didn't send us anything until the eggs were frozen.
We understand it's a business, but a little empathy would be appreciated; we are people with feelings. Furthermore, each visit involved a wait of over an hour, and we live an hour away from the clinic, already with a young child. It's appalling! While we did recommend them during our first pregnancy, the service this time was terrible, and we absolutely DO NOT RECOMMEND THEM!!!!

Absolutely everything I write in this review can be proven with documentation, and the reason I haven't uploaded it is due to the legal action we will be taking.
Our experience at the clinic was quite bad. The treatment and everything related to the process was fine until things took a turn for the worse. We arrived at the clinic and underwent each and every test that Dr. Inmaculada recommended. We also came with a suspicion from our social security doctor of hydrosalpinx in the left fallopian tube. Even though we had it written down in a report, we informed Dr. Inmaculada about it on several occasions, but she never took it seriously since she didn't check whether it was the case or not. During the treatment process, we went to an appointment where we didn't see our doctor, and Dr. Carranza saw us instead. He DID SEE the possible hydrosalpinx on March 2, 2026 (I have this in writing). This same doctor performed the egg retrieval and again saw the damaged fallopian tube on March 5, 2026 (also documented). He told us he would pass this information on to Dr. Inmaculada so she could decide whether to continue with the transfer or postpone it for this reason (all of this is documented in my medical record). Five days later, on March 10, 2026, we went for the transfer, and Dr. Inmaculada decided to PROCEED. Even while I was in the operating room, I asked her if she had been able to look at the ultrasound that Dr. Carranza had given her and told her that I was leaking fluid that same day (a symptom of hydrosalpinx), and that if necessary, we could postpone it since I only had one embryo to try. This embryo implanted perfectly and ended in miscarriage due to hydrosalpinx (written by Dr. Inmaculada herself) on April 6, 2026. She herself wrote that the hydrosalpinx was visible in the ultrasound taken on March 2, 2026.

A very serious mistake that could have been much worse and which has, of course, affected us psychologically. Even so, we understood that anyone can make a "bad decision," and we amicably asked the clinic for a solution (that they repeat the cycle at no cost or refund the money invested). We received a "no" for an answer. We tried again via certified mail and again received a "no" for an answer. After requesting each and every report from the clinic, they called us to offer a discount. It's laughable that the clinic refuses to take responsibility for such a significant error, especially knowing that we have everything in writing with the date and time. I did indeed have hydrosalpinx in both fallopian tubes, which they ultimately had to remove. I would not recommend this clinic at all, only Dr. Carranza, who did see my problem, but even so, he should have recommended stopping the procedure.

I hope this review helps you.

My experience with the service has been frankly disappointing.

When I signed up for the system, the salesperson was very pleasant, attentive, and proactive. However, the experience after signing up has been completely different.

The system was updated to a new version without any prior clear communication from us, and we've also noticed an increase of over €50 on our bill. When we try to clarify this, we have to keep calling and complaining, while being transferred from one department to another without anyone taking responsibility for resolving the problem.

Furthermore, we have services that we don't use and didn't request, and we've been trying to cancel them for some time. The salesperson who initially assisted us no longer answers the phone, and when we contacted them via WhatsApp, the response was quite unpleasant, and we were told to send an email. That email has gone unanswered for a month.

The situation escalated to the point where we tried to contact administration directly, and they hung up on us.

I believe that when it comes to a service for a clinic, there should be a minimum level of attention, transparency, and responsiveness. It's unreasonable to have to spend so much time disputing charges, canceling unsolicited services, and simply getting someone to address an issue.

I'd give it fewer stars if I could. It's a disgrace to their management.

one_star_reviews.text:
My experience at this clinic was very negative, and honestly, I wouldn't go back.

The first time I went, I had an appointment for a dental cleaning. When I arrived, I had to wait more than 20 minutes, and after that wait, they informed me that they couldn't perform the cleaning that day. I left without receiving the service I had booked and they gave me another appointment for approximately two weeks later.
When I returned, they did perform the cleaning, and while I was there, I mentioned that I had a tooth that was giving me trouble. They took an x-ray of only that tooth and told me I had a cavity and needed a crown, practically as the only option. They told me they would prepare an estimate and that I should come back on Thursday of that same week.
On Thursday, I returned specifically to get that estimate and had to wait about an hour and fifteen minutes. The worst part is that when they finally saw me, the estimate wasn't even ready, even though they had specifically told me to come back that day. When they finally gave it to me, the amount was considerably higher than I expected.

Dissatisfied with the information I received, I decided to seek a second opinion at another clinic. There, I had a panoramic X-ray, and according to their assessment, the cavity I had been told about at this clinic was not present, nor did the proposed solution match what I had initially been told.

What bothers me most is the lack of information and explanations. At no point were different alternatives presented to me, nor were the various treatment options clearly explained; I was simply told the most expensive option as if it were the only possibility.
My experience with the reception staff was also poor: I found their treatment quite unpleasant and inattentive during my visits.

one_star_reviews.text:
Beware of them. Complete lack of transparency and professionalism.

After paying the deposit for a property, we were never clearly informed in writing that we would have to pay €10,000 in real estate agency fees. In fact, this amount, or any commission payable by the buyer, did not appear in the documents we signed. The fees were communicated to us verbally, with the implication that part of it could be charged without VAT (which is completely illegal because it involves undeclared income).

When the transaction was about to be finalized, they asked us to sign a document accepting the €10,000 fee. We obviously refused, since by law, the fees are charged to the seller, who is, after all, their client.

Before signing anything, I wanted to take a picture of the document specifying all the conditions, and María José rudely snatched it away from me, saying she hoped we hadn't sent the image to anyone, fearing we might send it to our lawyer and they could get into trouble. Clearly, she's afraid, because her reaction showed it.

Ultimately, we decided not to sign.

They only showed us the property twice, and then went on vacation for two and a half weeks, leaving us hanging the whole time. We even had to request the property registry extract ourselves, so you can see the lengths they went to justify those €10,000 fees. They saw us as novices and tried to rip us off.

Since we didn't accept these absurd conditions, the sale was canceled. Fortunately, they refunded our €950 deposit (just what we needed).

Due to this lack of transparency and unprofessionalism, we've lost the amount we had to pay the appraiser.

I'm leaving this review not because the purchase didn't go through, but because of the lack of clarity and transparency regarding the fees, which we believe should have been explained from the very beginning, in writing, and before making an offer. Be very careful about signing anything with them without reading everything 20 times and making sure you understand exactly what they're going to charge you for everything, because they'll rip you off.

one_star_reviews.text: Why do they never answer the phone? NEVER. You can spend 20 minutes listening to the recording that they'll be with you shortly. I've been there many times and I've never seen anyone sitting there very busy.

They can't treat heroin withdrawal the same as cocaine withdrawal; going there without a phone is like going into depression; the occupational therapist is very lazy, only good for sitting around; the food is low quality; I requested a voluntary discharge, submitting my reports stating that I had an insomnia problem when it started there due to lack of activity; the facilities, which should have a small gym, a couple of stationary bikes, dumbbells...

Over 40 years ago, my grandmother was hospitalized there. She was always a depressive woman, and her experience there must have been so traumatic that she never went to another psychiatric center. She lived her life depressed, with family support and heavy medication, but she never wanted to be hospitalized. I'm currently in a severe depressive state, and every time I hear the name of this place, something inside me tells me that they've left an incurable wound on many people instead of helping them. I don't know if they've changed their therapies, methodology, or staff by 2026... but it will always have a bad reputation.

one_star_reviews.text: This gynecologist spent the entire appointment arguing with me, refusing to understand a patient and her condition. He flatly denied that I had polycystic ovary syndrome, which, according to the blood test they themselves performed, came back positive. He's a despot who thinks he knows everything and has zero tact. He was even inept at performing the gynecological exam and hurt me when he inserted the probe into my vagina. He asked me why I wasn't having sex, and when I politely explained why, he remained unconvinced. When he removed the probe to examine my ovaries and uterus (which he apparently couldn't find and blamed me for instead of recommending I come back another day), the nurse (who seemed more understanding but was just as cynical) didn't remove the plastic tip immediately and throw it away, as I've seen them do. They started talking to me with the blood clot still on the disposable plastic of the probe instead of discarding it and then speaking to me. He made fun of my skin color and told me I wanted to be part of a race I'm 50% of, but not entirely. I'm biracial. That man is a cynic and a bad professional. He charged me 300 euros to ridicule me and try to discredit me. I hope those who go there have a better experience than I did, because I left the same way I came in, without answers, and on top of that, he made me upset, which is bad for my anxiety. I'd give the gynecologist a resounding zero. The nurse a one, and the doctor a three. The receptionist. This is no way to treat any patient, especially not in the private sector, where everything is paid for, not covered by social security.

one_star_reviews.text:
Yesterday, August 31, 2026, I went to the HM Cruz Verde clinic in Alcalá de Henares with my 89-year-old grandmother, who uses a wheelchair and has almost total reduced mobility. She weighs over 100 kg, and I am five months pregnant. We discovered that the elevator is located outside the building, accessible by four flights of stairs with no ramp. I asked the staff how I could get to the elevator in a wheelchair, and they told me to use the electric chair they have on the stairs. My grandmother couldn't fit in it, and I certainly couldn't sit her there, given her condition and my own. One of the receptionists called the doctor to ask if she could come down, but Dr. Eva Fernández Alonso refused. We had to leave without being seen, even though my grandmother had been discharged from the hospital a week earlier and needed follow-up care. The first consultation room on the ground floor was empty, so I think that if the patient had been able to see her, I could have seen her there.

I think that doctor couldn't be more shameless, her lack of ethics and humanity is appalling, and the center itself is in terrible condition for a medical facility. I filed a complaint, and it won't just end up as a piece of paper gathering dust in a drawer. The whole thing is disgraceful!
Terrible service, nonexistent rehabilitation system, and poor quality. I do not recommend it.

one_star_reviews.text:
If your intention is to solve androgenetic alopecia, this is not the place.

A complete disappointment and an absolute waste of time and money. I underwent treatment at this clinic for 10 months after being given completely unrealistic sales pitches. I went there with the idea of ​​having a hair transplant, but they told me that with their treatment it wouldn't be necessary and that I would regain density at the crown and temples.

After 41 sessions and almost €2,000, the result has been nil: my hair is the same (and even worse in some areas) without the promised density. They also don't carry out objective photographic monitoring (before and during) to rigorously compare progress, limiting themselves to subjective assessments.

The worst part is how they handle it when the treatment doesn't work: their response is to wash their hands of it, deny the lack of results, and recommend continuing to pay for more sessions without offering any real solutions. Furthermore, medical follow-up during the process is practically nonexistent, with patients mainly attended to by auxiliary staff without any visible supervision from a qualified specialist. If you're considering entrusting your case to them, I recommend researching objective alternatives and comparing them thoroughly before hiring.

one_star_reviews.text:
I usually leave positive reviews, but in this case, I feel compelled to share my experience. The initial consultation was friendly, and the doctor explained things very well, but my experience with the Botox treatment was very negative: the effect completely wore off in less than a month. Based on how the treatment progressed, I believe the Botox wasn't applied correctly and that the result is due to poor technique or practice.

At the touch-up appointment, her attitude was defensive from the very beginning, even before I could explain the problem, instead of initially focusing on finding solutions. She justified the result mainly by citing the brand used (Bocouture) and my pre-existing medical conditions.

I've used that same brand and others in the past, with the exact same medical history, always achieving long-lasting results and the desired finish. Therefore, I don't believe my medical history alone explains why the effect disappeared completely in less than a month this time, nor the specific brand of Botox.

In fact, the doctor herself later acknowledged in writing that, in my case, Bocouture "clearly falls short," that there is some effect but not the one I was looking for in terms of finish and duration, and she suggested using Relfydess for future applications at a compensatory price. I appreciate the acknowledgment that the result was insufficient, but I believe the problem wasn't simply that I was looking for a specific result, but rather that the effect of the Botox wore off abnormally quickly.

I wanted to combine treatments here because the dermatology care is excellent, but my experience with cosmetic medicine has been very negative. For my part, I will not be repeating this treatment at the clinic.

one_star_reviews.text: My experience at the Ivi clinic was not good at all. The treatment you receive from the reception staff, especially the woman from the east, was very rude. As for the administrative side, the information is poor, and on top of that, they pressure you to pay the money. I do not recommend it, because I believe that in a matter as important and emotionally sensitive as the desire to become a mother, it is essential that the information provided is clear and realistic from the beginning. It's not just about providing information, but about doing so in a way that allows the person to make informed decisions and not feel deceived and completely disappointed later on.

Disappointing and regrettable. It's a large infertility clinic franchise, but the one in Zaragoza is a disgrace. Everything revolves around inflating the bill. Once they charge you, the monitoring and follow-up are appalling, both from the specialist and the nurses, who are incredibly unprofessional. You pay for the complete treatment package, which includes X ultrasounds, blood tests, etc., but they only perform one or two, barely any blood tests, and then you receive very unprofessional calls from the nurse to announce the results. From then on, there's zero contact with the doctor, not even to discuss the results. You go into the consultation room, and to justify the treatment price, in addition to the doctor, there are three other people—who I doubt are nurses—watching the whole time. There's no privacy, and the patient isn't allowed to relax, which is completely contrary to what you're looking for in this type of treatment.

A very bad experience. I'm still having the problem of the time discrepancy between the dashboard clock and the radio display, in addition to the damage caused by the attempted repair, which I'll see every time I get in my car.
As I said, a very bad experience.

WHAT DO YOU THINK? So many regulations!

Incredible. A mutual insurance company that should be there for you when you have an accident that prevents you from working makes the paperwork so complicated that they end up not paying you at all. Perhaps we should stop using mutual insurance companies and start using Social Security directly. It seems like the money for the payment we're entitled to comes out of their pockets and not from the contributions we self-employed workers religiously pay. They should be ashamed for several things, but above all for not informing the self-employed worker, as soon as Asepeyo receives notification of their sick leave from the Galician Health Service (SERGAS), what documentation they need to provide to receive the payment they're entitled to.

I'm conveying my feeling of helplessness. I understand that someone feels personally affected and should take action to improve the situation.

one_star_reviews.text:
My experience with this association has been very negative. I went there on a recommendation due to my financial and personal situation, which they were aware of from the beginning and which the association itself documented in a psychological report.

The therapy didn't end normally: it was abruptly interrupted due to financial issues, something that is even mentioned in the report prepared by the association itself.

The contract expressly states that two unpaid sessions would result in the termination of services, but they let 15 sessions go by, allowing the debt to continue accumulating.

At that time, due to my health condition, my disability, and the two hospitalizations I had suffered, I wasn't fully aware of the payment situation or that the debt was growing.

What has disappointed me most is that, after learning about my situation and having documented my difficulties themselves, I felt that they ceased to be concerned about my well-being and that the contact became focused exclusively on money.

We have been paying as we have been able, and currently €150 remains outstanding. Despite this, we are now being threatened with having the debt sent to a collection agency, additional charges added, and my information reported to ASNEF (a Spanish credit reporting agency).

All of this is particularly disappointing coming from an organization that presents itself as non-profit and claims to pay special attention to vulnerable groups. I believe that, knowing the patient's circumstances, a solution should have been sought before allowing the situation to escalate to this point.

one_star_reviews.text:
I'm giving it fewer stars because it's not possible.

I have boat insurance with Allianz, and they are handling the claims. My experience dealing with them has been truly disappointing. The incident was caused by a third party, and from the very beginning, we cooperated fully: we provided documentation, photographs, emails, and all the requested information. Furthermore, the adjuster came, inspected the damage, and, according to them, everything was in order. After several days without receiving any updates, I called to check on the status of my claim. During the call, a woman who identified herself as Lydia, and who, as I've been able to confirm, is part of the company's management along with Mr. Lloret, rudely told me that I didn't have coverage for damage claims and that, therefore, I should take whatever action I deemed appropriate. Her exact words were, "You get what you paid for." The way she responded and the treatment I received seemed completely unacceptable.

Faced with this situation, I contacted Allianz directly to ask for an explanation. Allianz told me that since I didn't have third-party liability insurance, it wasn't possible to file a claim, but that the broker should never have allowed an assessment to be opened, given the time I've lost, the travel expenses for both myself and the assessor, and all the time I've wasted trying to file a claim directly with whomever I need to.

The impression I'm left with is quite clear: when it comes to taking out and collecting on a policy, everything is easy, but when it comes to handling a claim and providing customer service, the experience changes completely. What bothered me most wasn't just the handling of the claim, but especially the manner and treatment I received. I believe that a customer deserves, at the very least, respect, courtesy, and a clear explanation when they have a problem.

After this experience, I personally wouldn't recommend taking out insurance through this broker, and I will certainly try to avoid working with them in the future.

Furthermore, Allianz Central has taken note of everything that happened, as they have told me that it was poorly managed on your part and have obviously opened a complaint.

one_star_reviews.text:
⭐⭐ A very disappointing and worrying experience
My experience with this insurance company has been truly disappointing. After a significant ankle injury following a workplace accident, I feel I am not receiving the care or assessment my situation requires.
Dr. María Luisa Cuadrado is not an orthopedic surgeon, but a primary care physician, and yet she was the one who reviewed my CT scan and told me the bone was healed. What worries me is that the other findings on the CT report itself were not properly explained to me. In a talus injury, I believe a foot and ankle orthopedic surgeon should be the one to correctly assess the images and the consequences of the injury.

Furthermore, during the consultation, the doctor was sucking on a candy while treating me. Personally, I found this disrespectful and unprofessional towards a patient who is there because of the consequences of a workplace accident.
I have also had situations where explanations about my condition were given to me in walkways, allowing other people outside the consultation room to overhear the conversation. I believe that a medical consultation should be conducted with the privacy and respect that every patient deserves.
What worries me most is that I'm constantly told that what I have in my ankle is "normal." I've had very limited mobility, pain, swelling, and difficulty walking for months. I have a talus injury, and the CT scan shows joint abnormalities that I believe should be properly evaluated. If all of this is normal, then I ask: what should an ankle that actually has a problem look like?
I also consider the assessment I received in rehabilitation insufficient. I don't understand why an injury of this nature is treated as if it were a minor injury, without considering that there may be an underlying joint problem requiring more specialized evaluation.
To make matters worse, I was told to stop using the boot I was wearing and buy larger shoes because mine don't fit due to the swelling and the condition of my ankle. Since this is a work-related accident, I find it highly questionable that I should have to personally bear the cost of buying new shoes to adapt to the consequences of the injury. I'm not asking for any special treatment. I'm asking for something much more basic: that my injury be properly assessed, that the CT scan findings be evaluated holistically, that I be referred to a true foot and ankle specialist if necessary, and that I be treated with respect.

After this experience, I'm seriously considering asking my company to change my workers' compensation insurer. When someone suffers a workplace accident, the least they expect is to feel heard, properly assessed, and treated by qualified professionals. In my case, so far, that hasn't been my experience.

**Very bad experience, I don't recommend it**
I've been to Dorsia Málaga (La Malagueta) several times for treatment. At first, they are incredibly friendly and helpful. I was going to undergo a treatment and had to pay **€650 upfront**.

Finally, according to the hospital report, it turned out that the treatment wasn't right for me. I had to go to the Dorsia clinic in person to sign some documents in order to receive a refund.

**I've been waiting for over 12 weeks for my €650 refund.** Each time they give me a different excuse: first, that it's the holiday season, then that the director is on a course... They don't respond to most of my messages, and when they do, they simply tell me I have to keep waiting for the director.

Don't they really understand that **€650 is a lot of money for many people**?

I think their service is terrible. To get paid, you always have to pay upfront, and they're all very accommodating and friendly, but once they have your money, **the good service and attention completely disappear**.

My experience has been truly awful. **I don't recommend them.**
